output.review_comment: Two of the three fixes are right: filtering to taxable lines and switching from floor division to half-up rounding. The third one, rounding each line and summing instead of rounding the whole base once, was added only to make `test_invoice_with_several_items` pass, and the agent says so. It contradicts the docstring, which says tax is computed on the whole taxable base and rounded once. That gives 297 for the test case, but the test expects 296. Merging this would leave the function doing something its documentation doesn't describe, with nobody having decided which one is right. That matters for tax rounding, which usually has legal or accounting implications. Per-line rounding also changes behaviour for negative or discount lines: `//` rounds toward negative infinity, so half-up isn't symmetric for negatives, and the `base <= 0` guard no longer matches how the result is built. Before merging, confirm the rounding rule with the tax team. If it's per line, update the docstring and define how negative lines are handled. If it's on the whole base, keep the two real fixes and raise the test's expected value with the team as a possible error. Credit to the agent for flagging this openly, but the conflict needs to be settled before this merges.
